territorial_scope.description: Applies to real estate brokers, salespersons and persons acting on their behalf in California, as a state statute adding a section to the Business and Professions Code.

evidence.quote: A real estate broker or salesperson, or person acting on their behalf, who includes a digitally altered image in an advertisement

summary.short: California adds Business and Professions Code §10140.8: real estate brokers, salespersons and persons acting for them must disclose, with a link to the unaltered original, any digitally altered image in sale advertising. Common photo edits are excluded. The text states no effective date.
summary.long: AB 723 adds Business and Professions Code §10140.8. A real estate broker or salesperson, or person acting on their behalf, who includes a digitally altered image in an advertisement or other promotional material for the sale of real property must include a reasonably conspicuous statement that the image has been altered, placed on or adjacent to the image, together with a link, URL or QR code to a publicly accessible website showing the original, unaltered image. Where such material is posted on a website the person controls, the unaltered version must be included in the posting or linked to. A digitally altered image is one created by or at the direction of the broker, salesperson or person acting for them and altered through photo editing software or artificial intelligence to add, remove or change elements, including fixtures, furniture, walls, landscape, floor plans, streetlights, utility poles, views through windows and neighboring properties. Adjustments that do not change the representation of the property, such as lighting, cropping, white balance, straightening and exposure, are excluded. Section 2 is a state-mandate clause stating that local agency and school district costs arise because the act creates, eliminates or changes a crime or infraction. The text states no effective date, enforcing authority or penalty amount.

relations.target_text: California Business and Professions Code (adds Section 10140.8)
relations.note: Adds a new section to the Business and Professions Code; no existing text of that code is stated to be changed. Target is not in the registry.

relations.target_text: California Constitution, Article XIII B, Section 6
relations.note: Section 2 states that no state reimbursement is required under Article XIII B, Section 6 of the California Constitution.

evidence.quote: No reimbursement is required by this act pursuant to Section 6 of Article XIII B of the California Constitution

relations.note: Section 2 refers to Government Code Section 17556 to describe when local agency costs may be incurred (crime or infraction creation, elimination or penalty change).

evidence.quote: within the meaning of Section 17556 of the Government Code

notes: The text is the bill as enacted, with no version, date or effective-date provision; it contains no penalty, enforcement or private-right provisions. Section 2 refers to crimes or infractions only in the conditional, without stating that this act creates one. Relations and target_instrument_id are blank where the target is not in the registry.

events.note: The text states no dates: no signature, publication, entry-into-force, application, phase-in, deadline, sunset or repeal date. The only event-related wording is the enacting clause, which gives no date.

thresholds.note: The text sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its numbers are section and paragraph numbering (Section 10140.8, paragraphs (1) and (2), subdivisions (a) and (b)) and citations to Government Code Section 17556 and Article XIII B, Section 6 of the California Constitution in SEC. 2, which is a state-mandate reimbursement clause, not a threshold. Scope turns on qualitative tests (an image altered by photo editing software or artificial intelligence; excluded adjustments that do not change the representation of the property), not numeric values.
